definitions.type: average covariance of two exponential phases
definitions.definition:
For real alpha,beta,
M_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds,
eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).
The notation M_tau here means Mavg_tau; eta_tau is the family eta at timestep tau.

output.statement: For every tau>0 and alpha,beta in R, eta_tau(alpha,beta)=0 if alpha*beta=0. Otherwise |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|<=2*min(|alpha/beta|,|beta/alpha|) and |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|<=tau*min(|alpha|,|beta|).

argument.text: Fix tau>0, alpha,beta real. If either phase vanishes its exponential is 1 and the covariance is zero. In the remaining case assume L1: alpha*beta!=0. Define h(s)=exp(-i*alpha*s)-Mavg_tau(exp(-i*alpha*.)). Then eta=tau^(-1)integral_0^tau h(s)exp(-i*beta*s)ds. The elementary integral estimate |exp(-i*alpha*s)-exp(-i*alpha*r)|<=|alpha||s-r| gives |h(s)|<=tau^(-1)integral_0^tau |alpha||s-r|dr<=tau|alpha|. Consequently |eta|<=tau|alpha|. At s=0,tau the sharper integrals are each tau|alpha|/2, so |h(0)|+|h(tau)|<=tau|alpha|; also integral_0^tau|h'(s)|ds=tau|alpha|.

Integration by parts against exp(-i*beta*s), which has nonzero derivative factor -i*beta under L1, gives |eta|<= (|h(0)|+|h(tau)|+integral|h'|)/(tau|beta|)<=2|alpha/beta| by F001. The defining covariance is symmetric in alpha,beta; repeating both estimates with the phases interchanged gives |eta|<=tau|beta| and |eta|<=2|beta/alpha|. Take their minima, discharge L1, and include the zero-phase case already calculated. Universal introduction proves the output assertion.
